Postoperative Pain Assessment Model based on 
Photoplethysmogram and Convolutional Neural 
Network 
 Ji Yeon Yim and Hangsik Shin* 
 
Dept of Biomedical Engineering Chonnam National University, Yeosu, South Korea 
*hangsik.shin@jnu.ac.kr 
 
Abstract. In this study, we developed a model to assess postoperative pain 
using the spectrogram of Photoplethysmogram waveform. Spectrograms 
were generated using pre- and post-operative PPG waveforms, respectively, 
and pain evaluation models were developed based on LeNet-5 and AlexNet 
models, then model’s performance was verified. As a result, the area under 
curves of the developed LeNet-5 model and AlexNet were 0.774 and 0.801 
with spectrogram input, respectively, and they were higher than those of the 
existing pain assessment technique, surgical pleth index (0.709). This result 
shows the possibility of using Photoplethysmogram for postoperative pain 
assessment and it is expected to show higher performance through the 
advanced convolutional neural network-based model. 
 
Keywords: Photoplethysmogram, Classification, Pain Assessment, Machine 
Learning. 
 
1 Introduction 
 
Most surgeries involve tissue damage and pain. If the pain persists, the body has an 
extreme stress response that negatively affects the patient's prognosis and recovery. 
Therefore, opioids are used to relieve pain in patients suffering from pain [1]. However, 
over-administration of analgesics may delay postoperative recovery and reduce 
circulatory activity in patients. In contrast, under-administration of analgesics can 
increase the blood pressure and pulse rate of a patient due to pain, which can have a 
negative effect on the cardiovascular system. Therefore, it is very important to 
understand the pain level of surgical patients for the administration of appropriate 
amount of analgesic [2]. Pain is closely related to the response of the autonomic nervous 
system, and pain assessment techniques based on physiological signals have been 
continuously proposed. These techniques estimate the presence and severity of pain 
through changes in heart rate, pupil size changes, respiratory volume, and 
Photoplethysmogram (PPG) waveform [3-6]. SPI (Surgical Pain Index, GE Healthcare, 
ins., Chicago, IL, USA) is a promising pain indicator based on PPG signal [6]. SPI is 
the useful indicator in the clinic, and is calculated as a score from 0 to 100. SPI could 
be calculated by 
 
SPI = 100 – (0.67 × PPGAnorm + 0.33 × HBInorm) (1) 
 
where PPGAnorm is normalized PPG amplitude and HBInorm is normalized heartbeat 
interval. Methods based on specific features, such as SPI, are cumbersome to derive 
feature values known to reflect pain from PPG. Therefore, in order to improve this, the 
pain evaluation study that finds a feature automatically by applying machine learning 
has been recently performed [7, 8].
